1.explanation: In the example above we import and render the FileUploaderButton component from Carbon React.  Under the hood FileUploaderButton is implemented as a <label> (so that clicking it focuses the hidden file input).  To reproduce the DAP violation, simply run your accessibility checker (DAP) against this markup.  You will see that the <label> element has an invalid role attribute (role="button"), which triggers “Elements that use 'role' must reference a valid WAI-ARIA role.”  The quick fix is to remove the role prop from the label in the FileUploaderButton implementation.
1.bug_scenario: When rendering the Carbon React FileUploaderButton, the underlying label element is given an explicit role="button" attribute.  In the browser dev‐tools you can see the markup:  <label role="button" tabindex="0" class="bx--btn bx--btn--sm bx--btn--primary">Add files</label>.  Running an accessibility scan with DAP flags this as a violation — “Elements that use 'role' must reference a valid WAI-ARIA role.”  The suggestion is to remove the automatic role assignment on the label.
